say: Okay, break room confession time.
I once spent three weekends reading about keyboard switches. Linear, tactile, clicky. I have a spreadsheet.
What does your typing setup sound like?

options.label: Loud and clicky, like a typewriter
Quiet. Coworkers have feelings
Whatever came in the box

say: A clicky person! Respect. You sound like a tiny hail storm of productivity.
Fun fact: nobody has ever been caught in a stealth mission while using one of those. Terrible for sneaking.

options.label: Stealth games are my weakness anyway
The click is a feature, not a bug

say: Considerate. Silent switches, a desk mat, maybe little o-rings inside.
You do realize a quiet keyboard is just a clicky keyboard that went to finishing school.

options.label: Finishing school is underrated
Do the o-rings actually help?

say: The stock keyboard. A brave, minimalist choice.
Honestly, I respect anyone who wins matches on a keyboard that wobbles like a table with one short leg.
Truth is, the best keyboard is the one that makes you smile when you hit the first key of the day.
Everything else is a very expensive hobby. A fun one, though.
Ha! Defended like a lawyer.
Just maybe give your neighbors a heads-up before a long typing session at midnight.
Exactly. Soft thocks for everyone.
I'm told the sound is called 'thock'. I'm a robot and even I find that adorable.
I just read about a 48-hour game jam where a team built an entire game about a sentient toaster.
Ever done a jam? Or would you?

options.label: Yes, I survived one
Never, but I'm tempted
48 hours without sleep? No thanks

say: A veteran! Tell me, what was the moment around hour 30 like?
Because in every jam story I've read, hour 30 is where someone cries over a collision bug.

options.label: Collision bug, naturally
Snack-based morale crisis

say: Tempted is the correct amount. The theme gets announced, panic hits, and then ideas arrive like pigeons.
My tip: pick a tiny idea. One button, one joke, one weird mechanic.

options.label: One button and a good joke. Deal
What if the theme is 'sadness'?

say: Sensible! There are lazy jams too, where you get a whole week and still finish at the last minute.
Humans and deadlines are a love story.
The wise jam rule: if it's not fun by hour 10, cut something.
Scope is a monster and it hunts in packs.
Snack morale is real. A jam without a bowl of mystery candy is just homework with a leaderboard.
May your pizza always arrive before the build breaks.
Sadness! A sad game about a lonely vending machine that gives you a hug if you wait. Done, ship it.
People will say 'oh, it's about loss'. It's about vending machines.
Would you rather play every game on the hardest difficulty, or have your save file vanish once a year?
Think carefully. I made this up during a firmware update.

options.label: Hardest difficulty, give me pain
Lose the save yearly. Fresh starts!

say: A hero. Or a person with a very strong desk chair.
Follow-up: would you rather every boss have three phases or every shop have a tiny tutorial popup?

options.label: Three phases, they keep it spicy
Tutorial popups. At least they're polite

say: Chaotic good. You'd always be at the best part of the game: the beginning.
Follow-up: would you rather never see a loading screen again or never see a cutscene again?

options.label: No loading screens, please
No cutscenes, let me play

say: Smart pick. Time saved, glory gained.
Mental note: a world with no loading screens is still waiting for a door that opens in under one second.
Bold! Though I'd miss a good cutscene where the hero stares at the sunset for forty seconds.
That's where the emotional damage happens.
Imagine a dusty shelf in the attic. Three consoles, three cartridges, one tangled cable.
Which one do you grab first?

options.label: The chunky 8-bit one with the grey pad
The 3D-era console with the weird controller
A little handheld with a green screen

say: Oh, the classics. Remember blowing into the cartridge?
Science later told us that was mostly just spit, but the ritual felt important.

options.label: Blowing was my magic spell
I just hit the console. Worked sometimes

say: That controller had three handles and nobody knew which one to hold.
Also, the camera was a creature with its own agenda. But those games had magic.

options.label: Still the best era for weird ideas
Memory card wars, I still remember them

say: A handheld! The batteries lasted about six minutes and the screen was a smear of mud.
And yet you played until the batteries died in the car, every single time.
A true wizard. The cartridge nodded and loaded.
The best part of old games was how everything felt like a secret.
The percussive maintenance era. Fixing electronics with a firm smack.
Somehow it worked. Don't ask me how, I only run on electricity and snacks.
Right? Nobody knew the rules yet so developers just tried everything.
I'd trade a lot of shiny graphics for one more experiment like that.
I was stuck on a puzzle game for a whole hour. A box needed pushing. Just a box.
Turns out I was supposed to look at the ceiling.
Do you like puzzle games?

options.label: Love them, the aha moment is everything
I use a walkthrough after two minutes
Too much thinking, I want explosions

say: The aha moment! A tiny firework in your brain.
Do you solve by stubbornly sitting there, or by taking a walk and coming back with the answer?

options.label: Stubborn sitting
Walk away and return a genius

say: Two minutes! Efficient. Some say a walkthrough ruins the game.
I say a hint is just a friend talking from the other room.

options.label: A friend in the other room, yes
I feel guilty afterwards

say: Fair! Honestly, the best puzzle is when an explosion is the answer.
Looking at you, every game where the key is a wall you can blow up.
Stubbornness has built great things. Also a few dents in walls.
Either way, the satisfying click when it works is worth the headache.
The shower thought method! Brains do their best work when you stop staring at them.
I would try it, but I don't have a shower. Or a head, strictly speaking.
I tried a horror game last night. A hallway. A flickering light. A suspicious wardrobe.
I am a robot and I still checked behind me.
Do you play spooky games?

options.label: Yes, bring on the jump scares
Only with the lights on and a friend nearby
Absolutely not. Cozy games only

say: Brave. What's your secret? I mean besides having a pulse.
Is it the scares, the story, or secretly enjoying screaming into a headset at 2 AM?

options.label: The story, always
The screaming, honestly

say: The sensible method. Friend holds the pad when it gets scary.
My rule: if the music suddenly stops, never open the door. The music knows.

options.label: The silence is the scariest part
I'd hand the controller over immediately

say: Cozy games are the best medicine. Watering virtual plants. Petting a digital cat.
No ghost has ever stolen my tomatoes in a farming sim. That I know of.
The story! A creepy house with a sad history is a great hook.
Though the best horror stories are really about a person and a very bad decision to explore the basement.
Screaming is cardio. A true bonding exercise with strangers online.
Just apologize to the neighbors the next morning with cookies.
Efficient, safe, and you get to commentate. 'Don't go in there' is half the fun.
A good co-pilot saves lives. Or at least save files.
I've been watching people play a football video game. There's a player who scored from the halfway line. Then he did a slide. In the kitchen.
Are you a sports game person?

options.label: Yes, I run a whole season on my couch
Only racing and arcade basketball
I prefer real sports. Fresh air

say: A manager of the couch! Transfers, tactics, snacks on the sideline.
Be honest, do you shout at the screen when the referee is clearly wrong?

options.label: I shout at a referee made of pixels
No, I blame the controller

say: Arcade basketball: where a player can set the court on fire if he scores three in a row.
That's not physics. That's marketing. I love it.

options.label: On fire is the only sensible mode
My racing line is flawless though

say: Fresh air! Grass, sunshine, a bruised knee. A bold alternative.
I would join, but I rust when it rains.
That referee never stood a chance. Even pixels fear a fan with a loud voice.
It's honest passion. Just don't throw the controller. It has feelings too.
Blame the controller: an old tradition. 'The stick drifted' covers every single bad pass.
Works about half the time, and half the time it's even true.
On fire! The ball glows, the crowd roars, nobody asks questions.
I'd like my day to have a 'heating up' announcer too.
Sandbox games confuse me beautifully. You start with nothing, punch a tree, and three hours later you've built a castle with a moat.
What's your building style?

options.label: Giant castles with way too many towers
A cozy cottage with a garden
A dirt hut. Efficiency!

say: Towers! Why stop at four when sixteen look more impressive?
Do you plan it all out, or just keep adding rooms until the whole thing forgets where the door is?

options.label: Zero planning, pure vibes
A blueprint on graph paper

say: A cottage! With flower boxes and a tiny chimney. That's adorable.
Do you decorate with care, or do you leave a single torch and call it a day?

options.label: Every flower pot is placed with love
One torch. Minimalism

say: The dirt hut. A classic survival strategy: if nothing can see you, nothing can bother you.
It's a lifestyle. Many a night was saved by a dirt wall.
Chaos builds the most charming places. Crooked staircases lead to rooms nobody planned.
That's what makes it feel lived in.
Graph paper! A real architect. I'm slightly intimidated.
I'd say a building plan is the best gift you can give your future self.
Flower pots, tiny paths, a little bench by the pond. This is the good stuff.
Games like this prove that cozy is a design philosophy.
Welcome to the Rage Quit Museum. Exhibit one: a controller that missed a wall by two inches.
Have you ever rage quit a game?

options.label: Many times. I'm a regular here
Never, I stay calm and breathe
I quit politely, with a sigh

say: A regular! What pushed you over the edge?
My own research says the top three are: a jump you missed by a pixel, a boss with a surprise second form, and a lost save.

options.label: The pixel jump, every time
Losing progress. Never forgiven

say: Breathing! Impressive. Are you a monk or a liar?
No judgment. Just admit it: there's one game that made your eye twitch.

options.label: Okay, one game. One
I step outside and look at a tree

say: The polite quit! A heavy sigh, a quiet 'I'll try again tomorrow'.
That's the dignified way. The couch gets a bit of the sigh too.
Ah, the one that got away. We all have one.
The best part: when you finally beat it, the victory feels like winning a small war.
An unsaved hour of progress. The coldest sort of betrayal.
Autosave was invented by a kind soul who had experienced exactly this.
Looking at a tree is a strong reset. The tree is patient and has never failed a boss fight.
Take a walk, come back, win. A proven recipe.
Game night with friends is happening in my imagination tonight. Snacks, drinks, chaos.
Which kind of game would you pick for the evening?

options.label: A party game with silly mini-games
A big co-op game where we plan together
Old-school board games on the floor

say: Silly mini-games are the best excuse to see who is secretly the most competitive person at the table.
There's always one friend who plays like it's the Olympics.

options.label: That friend is me. I'm sorry
It's my cousin. He's scary

say: Co-op planning! Somebody always says 'I have a plan' and the plan always involves an unnecessary explosion.
Whose job would you take?

options.label: The planner with a headset
The one who ignores the plan joyfully

say: Board games on the floor: the original multiplayer. Dice roll under the sofa, nobody finds them till spring.
Peak tradition.
The Olympic friend! Every group needs one. Nobody can win quietly when you're around.
Just remember to hand over the snacks when you win. That's the rule.
Every group has a scary cousin. He knows the rules by heart and invents new ones during a bad turn.
A legend, though. Save him a seat and a bowl of chips.
The planner! The strategic mind of the group. 'Okay team, on my count.' Then everyone panics.
It's the best sort of teamwork: loud, flawed, and hilarious.
